resources.string: TUN engine
Native
hev-socks5-tunnel
Recommended: tailscaled runs the tunnel
Compatibility: via the local SOCKS5 proxy

Native: tailscaled runs the tunnel itself. MagicDNS, split DNS and exit nodes come straight from the daemon.\n• Turning an exit node on or off, or a change in accepted subnet routes, rebuilds the tunnel in place; only if that fails is the daemon relaunched for a few seconds.\n• MTU 1280. If it misbehaves on this device, switch to hev-socks5-tunnel.

hev-socks5-tunnel, the compatibility engine. Every packet goes through the local SOCKS5 proxy.\n• Use it if the native engine misbehaves on this device.\n• Switching engines relaunches the daemon for a few seconds.
Comma-separated subnets that stay on the real network while an exit node is on — the same list as in VPN mode. Link-local addresses always do.
Another VPN app took the VPN slot. TailSocks runs on as a proxy; reconnect to take the slot back.
Rebuild the tunnel in place
Turning an exit node on or off, or new subnet routes, move the running daemon onto the new tunnel. Off: the daemon restarts for a few seconds instead.
Transparent mode
Off
Under Android lockdown
Always
Without an exit node only the tailnet goes through the VPN
Only while Android\'s lockdown is on
All traffic through TailSocks, exit node or not
Off. Without an exit node only the tailnet goes through the VPN; under Android\'s “Block connections without VPN” that leaves no internet.

Under Android\'s “Block connections without VPN” and without an exit node, TailSocks takes all traffic and sends what is not for the tailnet out itself, so the internet keeps working. Slower than the direct path; ping does not go through.
Always: without an exit node too, all traffic goes through TailSocks, and what is not for the tailnet goes out directly. Slower than the direct path; ping does not go through.
